conviction_note: The bar is the company's own Q2 guide (adj. EPS -$0.03 to -$0.01, adj. operating income $10-20M, revenue down high single digits, gross margin flat). Counterparty prints since 7 Aug point both ways: Dick's and Academy weak/promotional, Nike North America wholesale +9%, Columbia and adidas firm, Puma EMEA weak. Inside the guide most of these are already expected. A ~40%-of-float short with 6 days to cover sits against an 11% 20-day run-up. So p_up stays at 50 and the scaled number is 0, while the findings sum to +0.1. The two measurements agree that there is no edge. abs_move is 10.5 (option-implied 10.3, own median 7.8, raised for the crowded short and a possible FY guide change).
bar: Company Q2 FY27 guide, given 2026-08-07: adj. diluted EPS -$0.03 to -$0.01, adj. operating income $10-20M, GAAP operating loss $(11)M to $(1)M (https://finviz.com/news/379329/under-armour-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-results-maintains-full-year-profitability-outlook-while-updating-revenue-expectations). From the call: revenue down high single digits (NA and APAC HSD, EMEA LDD), gross margin flat year on year, adj. SG&A down LSD (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2944920). Prior-year Q2 revenue was $1.33B, so the implied bar is about $1.21-1.23B (my arithmetic). FY27 guide: revenue down MSD, adj. operating income $140-160M including about $70M of IEEPA refunds and about $35M of Middle East headwind, adj. EPS $0.08-0.12; FY consensus EPS $0.11 and revenue $4.96B (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/UAA). I could not source a Q2 street consensus from two agreeing places; a search snippet put Q2 EPS consensus near -$0.05/-$0.06 at the time of the guide. The company guide is the bar used.
positioning_check: Short interest: 65.1M UAA shares short at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 6.0 days to cover, up from 53.5M (6.8 days) at 2026-09-15, per Curved Trading quoted in a search result (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/uaa/short-interest/; direct fetch 403). Benzinga put it at 66.0M shares = 41.2% of float in Feb 2026 (https://www.itiger.com/news/2609545590, 2026-02-07); that crowded short is credited with the +20.4% squeeze on the Feb 2026 beat-and-raise. Borrow fee about 0.4% (curvedtrading snippet), so it is crowded but not hard to borrow. Options: skew_25d is null in the baseline, put/call OI 0.36 (call-heavy), ATM spread 67% of mid, so the implied 10.31% event move is indicative only. Holders: Fairfax about 42M shares (about 22%, Jan 2026), Frasers 16.6M Class A (8.78%, 13G event date 2026-09-24). Tape: +10.96% over 20d, +7.87% over 5d, up from $4.71 in early October.

findings.finding: UAA carries one of the most crowded shorts among liquid US apparel names: 65.1M shares short at the 2026-09-30 settlement (6.0 days to cover), rising from 53.5M two weeks earlier, roughly 40% of float. The last time a print beat a low bar (Feb 2026, adj. EPS $0.09 vs consensus -$0.02, FY guide raised), the stock squeezed +20.4%. That makes the right tail fatter than the history's 2-of-7-up suggests, on any print that holds the FY profit guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 beat-and-raise into ~41% short float: +20.38% (baseline). The May 2026 (-17.0%) and Aug 2025 (-18.07%) prints carried revenue/guide cuts, and the short did not cushion them, so the squeeze needs a non-negative guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, so the level is priced. What is not priced is how it reacts to the release. If the market fully expected a squeeze, the shorts would already have covered. Instead they added 11.6M shares in the second half of September, and options OI is call-heavy (P/C 0.36). The 20-day +11% run-up may be partial covering, which reduces the fuel.
findings.independence: Benzinga/iTiger Feb 2026 article giving 41.22% of float short and tying the +20% day to the short (https://www.itiger.com/news/2609545590). Different data vendor, earlier date.

findings.finding: Frasers Group (Mike Ashley) disclosed a new 8.78% position in UAA Class A, 16,576,500 shares, on a Schedule 13G (passive) filed 2026-10-01 with event date 2026-09-24. Together with Fairfax's ~22%, that puts about 30% of Class A with two value/strategic holders and shrinks the true float behind the short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No earnings print has followed a Frasers stake. The stock went from $4.71 (early Oct, around the disclosure) to $5.415 now.
findings.why_not_priced: Widely reported on 5-8 Oct (Retail Gazette, City AM, FashionUnited), so the existence of the stake is priced. It is a 13G, not a 13D, and Plank's Class B holds ~65% of the vote, so no bid is in the price and none is expected in the window. What remains is float tightening, which feeds the positioning finding above.
findings.independence: https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/sports-direct-frasers-stake-under-armour/ (press coverage of the same filing, so not independent of the fact).

findings.finding: Dick's Sporting Goods (UA's largest US wholesale account, now with Foot Locker) said on 2026-08-25, after UA last spoke, that the athletic footwear and apparel marketplace became 'increasingly promotional' as Q2 (May-Jul) progressed. It cut FY adj. EPS to $11-12 from $13.5-14.5 to stay price-competitive. UA's FY27 gross-margin bridge assumes lower discounting and its Q2 guide assumes flat gross margin. Plank had flagged the promotional market from late May on the 7 Aug call, so part of this is inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin and revenue misses drove the -17.0% (May 2026) and -18.07% (Aug 2025) prints, per the baseline and the cited coverage of those prints.
findings.why_not_priced: A counterparty print after UA's guide. If UA had already absorbed this, the stock would not have run +11% in 20 days into the print. The counter: Plank said the same thing on 7 Aug, so it is a known risk to a flat-margin guide, not a surprise.
findings.independence: UA's own call, 2026-08-07, on the market being 'increasingly promotional' since late May with heavy discounting in Europe/UK (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2944920). Same direction, but it is the company's own statement and so already in the guide.

findings.finding: Nike's FQ1 FY27 (Jun-Aug 2026, reported 2026-10-01) showed North America revenue +2% with NA wholesale about +9% while NA Direct fell about 6%. Nike is reclaiming shelf at the same sporting-goods wholesalers where UA guided North America to a high-single-digit decline in Q2. That is a share-shift risk for UA's wholesale order book.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UA North America (~55% of revenue) shortfalls were the driver of the 2025-2026 down prints (Q1 FY27 NA -9%).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy. Nike regaining wholesale is a widely read theme, and UA's NA HSD-decline guide may already embed it. If the market believed it hit UA's quarter, UAA would not have rallied from $4.71 after 1 Oct.
findings.independence: Stockhub breakdown NA wholesale $2.981B +9% (https://stockhub.kr/en/insights/view_1790895170625_s9p6gsq60). It reads the same Nike document, so not independent.

findings.finding: Academy Sports' Q2 (May-Jul 2026, reported 2026-09-09): comps -0.4%, transactions -5.3%, apparel division about flat and footwear -1.0%, with consumer spending 'pressured, particularly among lower-income households'. A second mid-tier sporting-goods channel was soft in the months that overlap UA's July-September quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As above: NA demand has been the line UA moves on.
findings.why_not_priced: Soft demand is inside UA's guide (Q2 NA HSD decline, 'challenging consumer environment'), so this mostly confirms the bar rather than moving it. Academy also raised its EPS guide, which tempers the read.
findings.independence: Dick's 2026-08-25 promotional comment (separate retailer, different document), filed above.

findings.finding: Circana's independent US series for the three months to September 2026 (released 2026-11-02): footwear dollar sales flat, units down mid-single digits, running +~10%, soccer up double digits, fashion footwear under pressure, and a flat holiday expected. Industry dollars are stable rather than collapsing. UA's guide for a high-single-digit decline therefore implies continued share loss, not a market problem.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No UA reaction measured against Circana releases.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out three days before the print and few read it for UA. It is a footwear-only industry proxy, while UA's footwear is roughly a quarter of revenue. It neither moves the bar much nor is it company-specific.
findings.independence: Columbia's US wholesale commentary (different source), filed below. Neither is UA data.

findings.finding: European peers since UA spoke diverge. Puma (2026-10-30) posted Q3 EMEA -11.5% currency-adjusted, citing weak European demand from Middle East spillover and softer wholesale partners. adidas (2026-10-29) posted group sales +9.4% and an operating profit above €1bn and confirmed a raised outlook. UA guided Q2 EMEA to a low-double-digit decline, which sits between them.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EMEA was UA's growth region (+12% in Q1 FY27). A swing there has not been the stated driver of a UA reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: UA's LDD EMEA guide already embeds a weak Europe, and EMEA is about a fifth of UA revenue, so the net effect on the company is small. The Puma side suggests the guide is realistic; the adidas side suggests brand-specific share.
findings.independence: adidas Q3 2026 coverage (https://www.teleborsa.it/AMP/News/2026/10/29/adidas-trimestre-record-con-utile-operativo-oltre-1-miliardo-confermato-l-outlook-rivisto-al-rialzo-41.html), which points the other way. Net about 0.

findings.finding: Columbia Sportswear (2026-10-29) said US wholesale Fall '26 orders increased but shipped later. It also guided 1H 2027 wholesale to grow mid-single digits in the US and globally on a larger Spring '27 order book. US sporting-goods/outdoor wholesale buyers are placing bigger spring orders, a modest positive read for UA's spring order-book commentary, which typically comes with the November print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UA's Feb 2026 +20% came with 'improving wholesale engagement' commentary. Order-book tone has mattered for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a peer in an adjacent category (outdoor) with partly different accounts, so the transfer to UA is uncertain. The stock's +7.9% in the last five sessions may partly reflect peer prints like this one.
findings.independence: Columbia CFO commentary on SEC (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050797/000105079726000148/cfocommentaryq32026_vf.htm). Same company, so not independent.

findings.finding: UA's 10-Q for the quarter to 2026-06-30 (Note 8) shows that the ~$70M IEEPA refund benefit was recognized in Q1 COGS, that $8M of refunds reduced inventory carrying cost, and that ~$13M of expected future refunds sat in prepaid/other current assets. The refunds are therefore mostly already booked. Q2 carries at most a small residual tailwind through inventory sell-through, and the refund is not a new Q2 surprise the way it was at other apparel names.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 FY27 refund landed with a revenue cut and the stock fell -4.53%. The refund did not carry the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in the 10-Q and in the FY guide, so it is priced. It is filed because the sweep flagged the tariff refund as a possible Q2 flatterer, and the primary document says it is largely behind the company.
findings.independence: Retail Dive on the FY27 profit guide relying on the $70M refund (https://www.retaildive.com/news/under-armour-counts-on-tariff-refunds-help-rebound/819943/).

baseline_tension: The +11% 20-day run-up (from $4.71 in early October) means expectations rose into a print where 5 of the last 7 reactions were down. The ~40%-of-float short pulls the other way, with skew unavailable and call-heavy OI. My mixed counterparty evidence neither confirms nor fights the run-up, so p_up stays at 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): Dick's promotional finding -0.8 -> -0.6, Nike shelf-share proxy -0.5 -> -0.4.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide is expected): Academy soft-demand finding -0.3 -> -0.2, because UA guided NA HSD down and called the consumer challenging.
Lesson 2 (one-off without a path to the guide): the IEEPA refund residual +0.2 -> +0.1. The refund was recognized in Q1 and is already in the FY guide.
Lesson 5 (proxies filed small, not dropped): Circana, Puma/adidas and Columbia kept at their small draft sizes.
Lesson 1 and the core (p_up carries the uncertainty): p_up stays at 50 and abs_move stays at 10.5. The sum moved from -0.2 to +0.1 and expected_move_pct stays at 0.
